newsitem.title: USA: Boise Cascade, Willamette report weaker results.
newsitem.headline: Boise Cascade, Willamette report weaker results.

text.p: Paper and forest products companies Willamette Industries Inc. and Boise Cascade Corp. reported sharply lower profits Monday, hurt by a depressed paper market.
Boise Cascade Chairman George Harad said the poor market conditions were partially offset by good results in Boise Cascade Office Products and building products.

Boise Cascade reported fourth quarter profits of $2.1 million, down sharply from $70.4 million a year earlier. However, after deducting for prefered dividends, the company incurred a loss of 16 cents per share vs. a profit of $1.07 per share a year earlier.

Boise Cascade Office Products, which is 83 percent owned by Boise Cascade Corp., reported net income fell slightly in the fourth quarter to $14.5 million or 23 cents a share from $14.8 million or 24 cents a share a year ago.
Revenues rose 48 percent, however, to $557 million.

"We had strong revenue growth in the quarter, including more than $50 million of same-location sales growth, compared with the same quarter a year ago," said Pete Danis, president of Boise Cascade Office Products.

Portland, Ore.-based Willamette reported fourth quarter earnings of $27.3 million, or 50 cents a share, down sharply from $130.7 million, or $2.37 a share, a year earlier. Revenues dropped to $837.6 million from $949.97 million.
The company said fourth quarter prices for unbleached paper grades ended their fall and markets were beginning to rebound as inventories tightened throughout the quarter.

Corrugated box prices were down marginally from the third quarter, and prices for Willamette's major converted fine paper products -- computer forms and cut sheets -- were down about 5 percent from the third quarter.
Willamette said its building materials markets languished during the quarter as well, although plywood prices were at their highest point of the year during the fourth quarter.
In a statement, Willamette Chief Executive Officer Steven Rogel said the company expects a rebound this year.

"While we're entering the new year with prices in most product lines significantly down from levels of a year ago, we feel that they have reached a cyclical trough," he said. "Inventories for our major paper product lines are also down, setting the stage for improvement in 1997."
Boise Cascade's stock fell $1.875 to $36.125, while Willamette fell $1.75 to $67.625. Boise Cascade Office Products stocks rose 25 cents to $21.25.
